# Real analytic division and germ rings

The source is [Bochao Kong's LocalComplexGeometry](https://github.com/BochaoKong/nullstellensatz)
at revision `029697242294aea7989bf5d391199696a43490df`. The Apache-2.0 license
is retained verbatim in `LICENSE`; copied source areas and adaptations are
listed in `NOTICE`. No dependency is added to the Lake configuration.

## Definitions and statements

`AnalyticGerm n` is the subring of Mathlib's neighborhood function germs
whose elements have actual representatives analytic at the real origin.
Germ equality means equality on some neighborhood. Evaluation is actual
evaluation at the origin. Units are characterized by a nonzero central
value, using an analytic reciprocal on a neighborhood. There are no formal
power series or existence assumptions standing in for convergent germs.

Linear coordinate pullbacks use genuine continuous linear equivalences.
Nonlinear analytic pullbacks use continuity at the origin to descend actual
composition to neighborhood germs. They preserve ring operations.

Weierstrass division uses real convergent coefficient series and a Neumann
inverse. Quotient and remainder uniqueness make the remainder map intrinsic,
additive, and linear over the lower-dimensional real analytic germ ring.
Its kernel is exactly the ideal generated by the actual prepared polynomial.
The quotient has the explicit basis `1,y,...,y^(d-1)`. Degree zero is allowed;
in that case the prepared polynomial is `1` and the quotient is the zero ring.

Rückert's theorem is proved by induction on the number of real variables.
The zero-dimensional ring is isomorphic to the real field. A nonzero germ
can be made regular in a distinguished variable by actual real linear
coordinates and real preparation. For any ideal containing that germ, its
remainder image is a finite module over the preceding Noetherian germ ring;
the kernel ideal is generated by the prepared polynomial. A finite image
generating set together with that polynomial generates the original ideal.
Coordinate equivalence transports finite generation back. Noetherianity is
the conclusion of this induction, never an assumption about the target ring.

Consequently, every family of germ equations has a finite subfamily with
the same ideal, and the same finite subfamily controls zero equalities after
every ring-homomorphic or analytic pullback. These are germ statements. They
do not assert one common neighborhood for arbitrarily many representatives.

Multiplication by any analytic germ acts on the actual rank-`d` prepared
quotient. Cayley--Hamilton gives a monic annihilating polynomial of degree
exactly `d`, with coefficients in the parameter-germ ring. Choosing analytic
representatives of its finitely many coefficients produces an actual monic
analytic polynomial relation on every nearby prepared root. This is a
necessary relation for projected values; no converse or surjectivity of a
real projection is asserted.

`analytic_fiber_minima_polynomial` uses division to replace a finite family
of analytic sign conditions and the analytic objective by their exact
polynomial remainders on the zero fiber. On a single fixed box this retains
the universal comparison with every admissible root in both directions.
The base parameters range freely; no analytic base curve is assumed.
Quantifier elimination and projected curve selection remain separate steps.

## External declarations

The relevant Mathlib statements, definitions, and typeclass assumptions were
inspected for neighborhood germs and composition, real analytic inversion,
finite coefficient evaluation and uniqueness, ideal spans and associated
elements, module remainders and kernels, finite generation, quotient
modules, finite power bases, and the characteristic polynomial. In
particular, the Cayley--Hamilton result applies over a commutative ring,
not just a field: the parameter-germ ring satisfies the actual commutative
ring and nontriviality assumptions. Its finite free quotient is supplied by
the explicit basis. The characteristic polynomial is defined by a matrix
of multiplication, is monic, and has degree equal to that basis's cardinality.
The matrix proof uses the adjugate identity and polynomial evaluation.

Concrete witnesses include nonconstant exponential units, singular regular
quadratic germs, the divisor `y²-z₀`, its nonzero cubic remainder `z₀ y`,
the infinite family `y,y²,...`, and nonlinear pullback by `(t²,t³)`.
The polynomial ideal `(X)` and its constant-coefficient remainder map also
witness the kernel-based finite-generation argument independently of germs.

The reproducible checks are:

```sh
lake build
lake env lean scripts/AnalyticPreparationAxioms.lean
lake env lean scripts/Axioms.lean
python3 scripts/index.py
```

The preparation-specific audit checks every copied preparation and real-germ
declaration and all external dependency roots transitively. Only `propext`,
`Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound` are accepted. This mechanical audit
supplements inspection of statements and definitions. There are no new
`sorry`, extra axioms, disabled linter options, or `native_decide` uses.

The general analytic gradient inequality remains open in this repository.
These results provide real analytic division, finite equation bases, and
finite-degree relations for projected fiber values. Selecting an analytic
curve in the projected set with global energy-level minimum comparisons
still needs proof. Complex root-existence and geometric finite-projection
claims from the source are excluded: they do not transfer to real scalars.
